title: Why Vultures Eat Rot: Stomach Acid at pH 1 🦅
description:
Why don't vultures get sick from eating rotten meat? Their stomach acid sits close to pH 1 and kills most germs, and the tough gut bacteria that survive, Clostridia and Fusobacteria, help digest the carcass.

topic: Why don't vultures get sick from eating rotten meat?
script: Vultures eat rotten meat that would kill you, and never get sick. Why? A carcass can be crawling with germs like anthrax, and the vulture keeps eating. First, the stomach. Vulture stomach acid sits close to pH 1, nearly as strong as battery acid. Most germs die right there. In one study of fifty vultures, scientists found five hundred twenty-eight kinds of bacteria on their faces, but only seventy-six made it to the gut. And the ones that survive? Tough, meat-eating microbes called Clostridia and Fusobacteria, germs that make most other animals sick. In a vulture, they're on the team, helping break down the meal. By cleaning up carcasses, vultures stop those germs from spreading. So be honest. Which grosses you out more, the rotten meat, or the gut full of flesh-eating bacteria?
key_facts: Vulture stomach acid is commonly cited near pH 1, killing most ingested bacteria (Smithsonian Insider: 'extremely harsh chemical environment'; TodayIFoundOut)
2014 Nature Communications study sampled 50 vultures (25 turkey, 25 black) in Tennessee (Smithsonian Insider)
On average 528 microbe types on the face, only 76 in the large intestine (Smithsonian Insider)
Gut dominated by Clostridia and Fusobacteria, flesh-digesting bacteria toxic to most other animals (Smithsonian Insider / Nature news)
Carcasses can carry pathogens like anthrax; vultures tolerate them and remove carcasses (TodayIFoundOut)
